notes.title: Reflections on 2024
notes.notes:
A lot happened in the past year. Many felt the impact of escalating geopolitical events, and I am personally somewhat anxious about my own wellbeing in the coming year. There is a space for games that speak to these issues, but RSOD is primarily a low-brow action game, so I will leave the political discussion at that.

For RSOD, the single most important milestone in 2024 was [url=https://code.onedev.io/RSOD]the release of its source code[/url] under a permissive license. Since June, the Git commit log has tracked every change to the engine, including:

[list]
[*]Projectile Weapons (Plasma Pup and enemy shotgun)
[*]Game maps as title screen backgrounds
[*]Continuous particle emitters (smoke barrels and rain)
[*]Improvements to UI, enemy AI, and bug fixes
[/list]
[h3]New Map: Hidden Valley[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/a6c452b6c2a9bf4587bb766522fd84b76d68e0bc.jpg[/img]
This is a work in progress. Anyone who tries to make a game with cyberpunk aesthetics will quickly come to the realization that the world we live in is quite cyberpunk already, thus the map looks like a place you might see in your town.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/9d041617ef308fdb986205bc9f7e28b2814a93d1.jpg[/img]
I'm proud of the architectural detail, which comes from that liminal space between minimalism and brutalism you see in a mid-90s FPS. This is a mid-2020s FPS, so I'd call it [i]nostalgic[/i].

The demo has been updated with all of these changes and more, so please give it a shot! Have a happy new year.

[b]List of changes[/b]
[list]
[*] Highlight the agent the player is looking at
[*] VTOL quick travel after the player gets implanted (this may be used for future missions)
[*] Give Gogol a 2-way entrance
[*] Default to 2x MSAA (This may lead to some breakage/white screens. You can change msaa to 0 in the settings, then restart the program.)
[*] Bug fixes
[/list]

[list]
[*] Removed a screen shake effect that nobody liked
[*] Increased hick turn speed
[*] Added particle effect to enemy shotgun
[*] Made the grocery district a little larger
[/list]
Fixed a bug that made destroyed objects continue to display on the minimap

A bunch of little changes 2 weeks after the previous update. Steam won't surface the game until a week before launch day, so it's not like anyone will notice. One of these changes is for [i]compliance[/i] and took close to 3 full days. It's enough to make me want to build my own platform.

In celebration of Pride Month, I did the gayest thing possible: the RSOD engine is now free/libre open source software and ready to receive your patches. You can check out the source code [url=https://code.onedev.io/RSOD]here[/url].

notes.title: Progress Report: 2023/09/02
notes.notes:
[h2]THE BASICS[/h2]

In the past month, I added three significant quality-of-life features to RSOD:

[list]
[*] Saving and loading
[*] Options menu
[*] Radar minimap
[/list]

It's no coincidence that I received this comment in a survey:

[quote]Have the possibility to change the controls for the qwerty keyboard.[/quote]

Well, anonymous playtester, check it out:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/7508e3d8b7e5219787bfa40c900bb6b39d7bba5e.png[/img]

Note that the game starts with default keybindings based on your keyboard layout, so if you have an AZERTY keyboard you will automatically have ZQSD rather than WASD, and this is reflected in the options menu.

[h2]HIATUS[/h2]

A typical FPS has more than 50 maps. RSOD currently has 8, so let's call it 16% complete. At this rate, the game will be finished in early 2034.

I intended the game's story to be a loud warning to Big Tech, but at present the experience feels a bit generic. Steam can't tell it apart from one of those glitchy Unity games with 1000 zombies that let you move around after you're dead (not as a zombie). For these reasons, I am putting the game on hiatus until it organically gets more wishlists.

The engine may still get updates as I prototype a dark fantasy game. (Send your ideas and other thoughts to support@microsm.space)

notes.title: Progress Report: 2023/08/01
notes.notes:
It's now August, midsommar in the northerly parts and midwinter in the southerly parts. As I was occupied for the past 3 months, development on RSOD stalled. However, I managed squeeze in a small content update to the grocery store in North Island. Go through the tunnel and check it out.

I got one survey response in July: [b]Xin chào, tôi muốn biết giá của bạn. (Hello, I would like to know your price.)[/b]

My response: [b]Đó là bí mật. (It's a secret.)[/b]

I find it rather depressing how much of Steam is bartering and commerce, so I won't overcharge.

The GLIBC issue is still on the radar, but thankfully it doesn't affect Windows users. You can expect more updates in the future.

notes.title: Progress Report: 2023/06/01
notes.notes:
It's now June, the start of summer in the northern hemisphere and a time for relaxation. The RSOD playtest remains available for your pleasure. It hasn't been getting a lot of survey responses, but I think these responses from May hit the nail on the head:

[b]Q: What did you like?
A: Girls able to do leg stretching

Q: What features do you think could be improved or added?
A: more options to progress the game[/b]

I also got a bunch of spam. 

As previously stated, there won't be any game updates for a while. I don't like the implication of "options to progress", as if the player is the one moving the game forward. The game should carry the player forward, not the other way around. It should be clear where the waypoints and objectives are. That will require more development, as the current build is more of a sandbox. I want this to be a narratively rich experience, so give me more wishlists and I can put more time into development.

By the way, I am aware of a GLIBC version mismatch for Linux builds. I will look into this in the coming months.

notes.title: Progress Report: 2023/03/01
notes.notes:
Over the last development cycle, a lot of the game's ambition was put on the back burner. Right now you just shoot things, but in the future there will be deeper character interactions. There is not a huge volume of players hungry for futuristic open-world gun games on Steam. Borderlands was a thing for a while, but people moved on to the next fad pretty quickly, and now AI is the hot topic in the gaming space. I am looking into ways to make characters more dynamic, and AI may have a role to play.

It's easy to fall into a pit of negativity when there is a lack of interest in your work, but some of my work on other projects is bringing greater fulfillment. If AI is meant to replace people, that says something for the value that people have. I may be flying solo on this project, but it's not my whole career, just a project that sets a high bar in terms of graphics and engine features. This is my Doom 3. You don't have to like it, but you have to admit it's impressive.

RSOD's most recent feature is an experimental third-person mode that's not quite ready for prime time. When it is ready, you'll have to see if you prefer the game in first-person or third-person mode. Seeing the character from behind might help you connect with him or her, in the same way that people see themselves from an outside introspective perspective. Third-person shooters have fallen out of fashion, but if it helps you see the character as a person (rather than a capsule collider with a gun for a head) then I would say the game benefits.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/5bb0eca2dd825fd8f0bd2f4dff938928f2309631.gif[/img]

In other news, Steam just added a content questionaire today that mirrors Google Play and will only serve to increase censorship. As RSOD is more likely to have strong adult content than any other shooter I can imagine, this makes me question the viability of Steam from a creative perspective, not just a financial one. There is distributing a game without making money, and then there is not distributing a game at all.

notes.title: Progress Report: 2023/01/01
notes.notes:
I originally planned to release RSOD in early 2023, but now it's looking like a "when it's done" release schedule. Thanks for all the feedback you have given on the playtest, which will remain open until the first demo is released. I can't say when that is, but perhaps this year.

I know my fellow millennials like pictures between the words, so here's a before-and-after screenshot comparison:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/3e58fe517a4dfeeb484b6fa492f465a298ffa595.jpg[/img]

You can see the addition of a HUD, vehicle headlights, clouds, more environment details, new shaders, and of course weapons.

Now, let me set the stage with a few words about scope, themes, and tone.

[h2]Scope[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/50a3a024e4ac534a322e44002a9af17a848988af.jpg[/img]

RSOD is a single-player open-world FPSRPG with a story. If the feature you want isn't in that sentence, it probably won't be in the game. Think Borderlands, Half-Life, and Ion Fury.

[h2]Themes and Tone[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41570668/2a5f4f27677dc19d62d60f4b5bc428b6f8e215f0.jpg[/img]

Almost nobody does cyberpunk just right. The way I imagine it, it's about hacking and killing for money, but mainly it's about sex. I want to create an amoral world where the player does whatever pleases him, her, or it (within the limitations of the software). A world that is fully adult in its humor and storytelling.

In my opinion, the best cyberpunk atmosphere of any game can be found in Dex, and its original creator died several years ago, so it's too late to tell him that. Dex is brightly lit and slightly futuristic, not the total grunge misery of Deus Ex and "dystopian" cyberpunk. I don't want to make something dystopian, I want to make something that gets you amped up at any time of the night to go do some fucked up shit.

I hope you understand that this isn't GTA and it's not made for teenagers. If you are intelligent and you enjoy the combination of serious topics and kinetic violence, this might be for you.
